concept: Design token interoperability, themes and modes

claims.text: A composite token contains named subvalues for related styling properties applied together; it is not merely an arbitrary group of independently organized tokens. (low confidence)

Resolve aliases after context selection and ordered overrides have produced the final token structure. The resolver allows deep alias chains but forbids circular references and requires the referenced type to match. (low confidence)

DTCG composite tokens combine multiple named sub-values in a predefined structure. Tokens Studio distinguishes these from its legacy generic composition token, which its guide recommends replacing with independently defined token types. (high confidence)

Resolver ordering is significant: later sets or selected modifier contexts override earlier conflicting tokens. Aliases must resolve after the ordered token structure has been flattened. (low confidence)

Cross-platform conversion can lose responsive typography behavior: the DTCG dimension definition permits a lossy fixed-size conversion when a target platform has no equivalent to relative root-font sizing. (low confidence)

Resolver portability has a boundary: same-document references are mandatory, but tools may decline local-file or remote-URI imports. Bundling through optional definitions can also fail to transfer across tools that ignore those definitions. (low confidence)

DTCG defines a platform-agnostic interchange format for design decisions; its purpose is to reduce bespoke integrations between design and development tools, rather than prescribe a particular authoring tool. (low confidence)

Contentful distinguishes modes as variations within token collections and defines a theme, in its own model, as a separate complete token set retaining the same structure. Treat this as an attributed convention rather than a universal definition of themes. (low confidence)

Tokens Studio documents a concrete composition limit: applying a composition token styles one layer rather than all child layers, and individual property tokens attached to Figma styles or variables do not appear as such in the Figma UI. (low confidence)

Contentful uses mode for contextual value variations, collection for tokens that share modes, and theme for the full set of collections; the article cautions that theme is also sometimes used to mean mode. These are the article’s working definitions rather than universal interchange terminology. (low confidence)
The DTCG Format Module 2025.10 is a stable Community Group specification, explicitly neither a W3C Standard nor on the W3C Standards Track. (low confidence)

In the DTCG format, a token type may be explicit or derived from a referenced token or the closest typed parent group; an undeterminable type is invalid, and tools must not guess it from the value. (low confidence)
Aliases let semantic names reference underlying tokens. Contentful and Aha! illustrate keeping usage-oriented names stable while changing the primitive values selected for a theme. (high confidence)

The resolver explicitly covers light, dark and high-contrast color modes, sizing contexts, and accessibility contexts such as reduced motion; it addresses repeated token values across combinations of contexts. (low confidence)

In the DTCG resolver, sets provide token sources and modifiers conditionally select sources through named contexts. Later sources override earlier occurrences, and the resolution order determines the final tokens. (low confidence)

The format requires tools to preserve extension data they do not understand, but recommends keeping extensions to optional metadata that is not essential to interpreting a token value. (low confidence)
Resolver conformance does not guarantee remote-file interoperability: same-document references are required, while tools may decline local-file or remote-network URI types. (low confidence)

Tokens Studio distinguishes its legacy generic composition token from specifically typed composite tokens. Its documentation recommends migration and describes difficult code transformations and known composition-token bugs; this documents a portability hazard, not a verified status of every linked bug. (low confidence)

In a 2024 Style Dictionary discussion, collaborator `jorenbroekema` recommends theme-specific semantic overrides and separate outputs for scalability, while requester lukasoppermann says manual file management is burdensome and unused CSS is not a major concern for that project. These are conflicting workflow judgments, not measured universal performance results. (low confidence)
Design tokens express design decisions independently of a target platform; an interchange file still needs translation into platform-specific outputs. (high confidence)
The DTCG Format Module defines a JSON interchange format intended to reduce bespoke integrations between token tools. Its publication status explicitly says it is not a W3C Standard. (low confidence)

Aliases let a named token reference another token. The format permits alias chains but prohibits circular references; the resolver also requires aliases to point to the correct type. (high confidence)

A mode can keep a semantic token name stable while changing its value for a context such as light or dark appearance. The DTCG resolver describes conditional token values using sets and modifiers. (high confidence)

A resolver document describes conditional values but requires external inputs to select contexts. Conforming tools validate inputs against declared modifiers and allowed context values. (low confidence)
